name: God Helmet: amygdala both sides, then hippocampus right (40 min)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shiva God Helmet software); signal templates licensed from Persinger & Koren
summary: Todd Murphy's two-phase Shiva God Helmet session: the amygdala burst-firing signal over both temporal lobes, then the hippocampal 'LTP' signal over the right temporal lobe only. The vendor expects 'deep calm, inner images, and possibly a sense of spaciousness' in phase 2; 40-minute version.
notes: 40-minute version (20 + 20 min, switching abruptly); the vendor also offers a 60-minute version (murphy-gh-amybi-hippr-60min). Four coils per temporal lobe in a cross centred near T7/T8 (an inference from 'four coils over each temporal lobe'); the field steps from coil to coil, 'clockwise over the left side, counter-clockwise over the right' as the vendor states, read with each side seen from its own side, so both sides step top, back, bottom, front (C5-TP7-T9-FT7 and C6-TP8-T10-FT8; an inference). An image caption on the vendor's session list says the signals cycle clockwise on the right side, which contradicts the text; this preset follows the text. The step time is unpublished (Murphy: one cycle takes 'a fraction of a second'), so 125 ms per coil (0.5 s per cycle) is used. The amygdala 'burstx' file is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) with 230 points, the point count of the published lab burst-firing pattern (which used 4-ms points; Ryczko & Persinger 2002), on the vendor's standard 3-ms points, so 0.69 s, close to the 'about 0.7 s' bursts Persinger's lab reported at 1 µT (Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009); then the 4-s silence: about 9 s of field per minute (the vendor states 9.6 s). The hippocampal 'LTP' file is proprietary; it is approximated by the project's Larson & Lynch theta-burst table (4 pulses at 100 Hz per burst) at the 5.4 Hz spectral peak the vendor reports for this signal, 4 bursts (0.6 s), then the vendor's standard 4-s silence; the burst count is a choice, and 0.5-ms points replace the vendor's 3-ms points because 100 Hz pulses need them. 1 µT follows Persinger's papers, which mostly report about 1 µT (10 mG); the vendor's own figures disagree (10-20 mG on one page, a 50 or 90 mG 'laboratory standard' on others). Fear or anxiety in phase 1 means stop. Murphy reports that irritability in phase 1 'is often a sign that the second phase will be especially effective'. Fear or anxiety in phase 2 means stop and never reuse this session. Not for people prone to anxiety. Persinger's lab reported more aggression and less trust after three weekly bilateral burst-firing sessions (Gillis & Persinger 1993). The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% with the hippocampal signal; if so, lower the intensity by one third. The 'hippocampus on the right' rule rests on a small Persinger-lab study (Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994: LTP-pattern fields over the right hemisphere were rated more pleasant than over the left). Vendor exclusions: epilepsy or seizure history, psychiatric conditions or medication, migraine, brain injury, drugs. Stop on any distress. Independent double-blind tests found no effect of the fields (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012).
setting: Darkness and acoustic silence (the vendor: 'silence, not just quiet'), blindfold or eyes closed; sit or lie relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. The vendor prefers night sessions on geomagnetically quiet days and a helper who can stop the session. No meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor rules: at most weekly, never on consecutive days; a series of up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break; not mixed with Shiva or Shakti sessions in the same weeks; try a session 2-3 times before changing it.
